newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian tribal guerrillas bomb train.
newsitem.headline: Indian tribal guerrillas bomb train.

text.p: Tribal guerrillas in the northeastern Indian state of Assam exploded a bomb and derailed six coaches of a passenger train on Monday, police said. There was no immediate report of casualties.
The guerrillas triggered a remote-controlled bomb as the Rajdhani Express train moved through Barpeta district, about 100 km (60 miles) west of the state's main city, Guwahati, police said.

"We suspect the Bodoland Liberation Tigers Force (BLTF) to be involved in the blast as they have been bombing bridges in the state for the last couple of days," a senior police official told Reuters in Guwahati.
The BLTF, which is seeking a separate province carved out of Assam for 600,000 Bodo tribespeople, bombed a train last December 30, killing at least 30 passengers.
Monday's blast came two days before the start of a 36-hour general strike called by Bodo student groups campaigning for a Bodoland province.
